items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: So I say okay find a recording of it, listen to Mr. Parker and the other horns

ctx.x: Okay, well for me the defining factor is how well one listens and perceives sound. And there is a very corny adage which is very true is if you can’t say it you can’t play it. So

my teaching over the years became less and less visual, meaning exercises out of a book, and more and more aural. And what I found was that another impediment to one’s learning ability was the ability to internalize the music and especially as a jazz player. Because you know when a drummer is playing the tune and when the drummer is just playing his licks. When you listen to somebody like Roy Haynes and hear how he orchestrates the tune, I mean it’s right there. Billy Higgins, Philly Joe, all the great drummers…
Yeah I was going to ask right at the beginning of this wonderful description you said, “aural.” I’m assuming you’re going A-U-R-A-L. Correct?
